newsitem.title: ERITREA: More than 90 percent turnout in Eritrean election.
newsitem.headline: More than 90 percent turnout in Eritrean election.

text.p: A total of 93.8 percent of all registered voters turned out to vote for a regional assembly on Saturday in the central region of Maakel around the capital, officials said on Tuesday.
Mekonnen Abraha of the local government ministry said a total of 140,601 people cast ballots out of 149,957 registered voters in the last of six elections for regional assemblies since January.
Each regional assembly will send representatives to make up an assembly to ratify a constitution for Eritrea.
"They (the people) have a high interest and motivation in their country's political affairs," said Mekonnen.
Each regional assembly has about 70 seats, except for the Southern Red Sea region which has 37 seats. Thirty percent of all seats are reserved for women.
"All six elected assemblies will now be officially opened by the regional administators, after which they will ratify their regional by-laws and elect chairmans and secretaries," Mekonnen said.
Eritrea, Africa's youngest nation, became independent from Ethiopia in 1993 after fighting a 30-year war with Addis Ababa.
